book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook would list the dimensions, indicators and goalposts, give the index formula, then aggregate. Here the whole pipeline is shown first at a 'bird's eye view' with made-up finished indices (0.7, 0.8, 0.9 -> 0.795), so the learner knows the destination before any detail; then the two skipped parts are marked with '?' and filled in (goalposts, meanings), and finally the full pipeline is rerun on India's real numbers, row by row, ending on the same geometric mean. The order works: answer first, then 'how did we get those three numbers'. It loses force at the end because two of the three India indices are never actually computed.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Show the full calculation once with ready-made numbers, then open each black box in the order the calculation needs it (indicator, goalposts, meaning, index formula), and rerun the whole thing on real data.

narration.density: About 16 terms (HDI, dimension, indicator, normalise, minimum/maximum value, nominal value, geometric mean, cube root, GNP per capita, PPP, life expectancy, mortality rate, expected years of schooling, mean years of schooling, index value, arithmetic mean, logarithm, UNDP, human development groups) in about 430 s, about 2.3 per minute; but the voice is fast (about 187 words a minute, no pauses over 1.2 s) and formula-heavy. Fine for UPSC/class 11+, too fast for school learners, especially the log step.

talmel_summary: Tight sync for a formula video: 17 of 24 changes land within 0.8 s of their word, and the calculation is written piece by piece on its own words (multiply, then cube root; numerator, then denominator; a red cross on 'will not work'). The picture mostly writes what is said (labels, table cells, English definition boxes) rather than showing what it means; the strongest visual moves are the converging arrows into one geometric mean, the curly brace folding two education values into one, and the green row frame that walks the worked example. Weak: band cut-offs never spoken, the long clamping rule reduced to a small cap, and two of three India indices never shown as numbers.

voice.notes: Fast (about 187 words a minute) and even, no pauses longer than 1.2 s; a teacher reading through a worked sheet. Formulas are read in full English words ('actual value minus minimum value divided by maximum value minus minimum value') and numbers digit-wise in English ('zero point seven nine five', '67.2 minus 20'). Signposts are short Hindi phrases ('chaliye', 'bat abhi ye topic khatam nahin hua'). Stress falls on 'geometric mean', 'normalize' and the problem line before the log formula. The long clamping rule (about 30 s, one run-on sentence) is the least clear stretch.

game_ideas.player_does: Is the 'HDI calculator' for a country: drags each actual value (life expectancy, schooling years, income) onto its goalpost ruler, then slides a marker to where it sits between min and max.
game_ideas.process_happens: The ruler shows the fraction filling (67.2 years on the 20-85 ruler fills 72.6%); for income the ruler is drawn in log steps ($100, $1,000, $10,000) so $6,590 sits at about 63%; the three fills become three bars that merge into one HDI bar by geometric mean.
game_ideas.win: All three index values and the HDI land within 0.01 of the true value, and the country drops into the right band (very high, high, medium, low).
game_ideas.lose: Using the linear ruler for income puts $6,590 at only 9% and HDI crashes; the game shows the log ruler beside it and asks why a rich country's extra dollar should count less. Putting a value below the minimum is clamped to 0 with a small 'floor' animation.
game_ideas.concept: dimension index = (actual - min) / (max - min), India health and education

game_ideas.player_does: Has a fixed budget of 'improvement points' to raise a country's health, education or income index, starting from a lopsided country (0.9, 0.9, 0.3).
game_ideas.process_happens: HDI is recomputed live as a geometric mean beside an arithmetic mean; points spent on the weakest dimension lift the geometric HDI most.
game_ideas.win: Reach a target HDI with the fewest points by fixing the weakest dimension first.
game_ideas.lose: Pouring points into an already-high dimension barely moves the geometric HDI while the arithmetic mean rises; the game shows the two means side by side so the learner sees why HDI punishes imbalance.

game_ideas.player_does: Places five country cards (made-up names with HDI values like 0.82, 0.633, 0.71, 0.49, 0.55) into the four UNDP bands.
game_ideas.process_happens: Each card snaps into its band and the band edges (0.550, 0.700, 0.800) light up.
game_ideas.win: All cards in the right band, including the edge cases at exactly 0.550 and 0.700.
game_ideas.lose: A card in the wrong band bounces back with the cut-off it crossed shown on a number line.

notes_questions.q: HDI ke teen dimensions kaun se hain aur har ek ko kis indicator se naapte hain?
Har indicator ki minimum aur maximum value (goalposts) kya hai?
Index value ka formula kya hai? India ki life expectancy 67.2 ho to health index nikaaliye.
Education index do indicators se ek kaise banta hai? 11.9/18 aur 6.7/15 se nikaaliye.
Income index mein log kyon lete hain?
HDI geometric mean se kyon nikalta hai, simple average se kyon nahin? 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 se samjhaiye.
UNDP ke chaar HDI groups aur unki cut-off values kya hain? India kis group mein hai?

checks_learned: A worked example that sets up a formula for several inputs must compute every one of them on screen; leaving x and y (or a tick) where a number belongs fails the check.
When a formula changes for one case (log for income), the script must say why in one plain line; 'the formula will not work here' without a reason fails.
Every number on screen (band cut-offs 0.800, 0.700, 0.550) must be spoken, or the voice must point to the table and name the band in use.
A made-up example ('maan lijiye') must not carry a real country's name or flag; use a fictional country or real data, not both.
Real statistics (HDI 0.633, rank 132 of 191, 67.2 years, $6,590) must carry the report year on screen.
Term check against the source: the voice and screen say 'GNP per capita' where the UNDP method uses GNI per capita; a glossary check should flag such near-miss terms.
A spoken rule with three cases (below min, above max, in between) should be shown as three cases (a value clamped at the floor, at the ceiling, and placed between), not as one small icon.
Speech rate above about 180 words a minute with no pause over 1.2 s through formulas should flag a pacing warning for school-level learners.

teaching_best.why: Bird's eye view first: a full calculation with ready numbers (0.7, 0.8, 0.9 -> 0.795) before any detail, so every later piece has a place to go.
'But the topic is not over': the skipped parts are named as open questions and marked with '?' on the existing picture.
The goalpost rule is spelled out as three cases (below min, above max, in between), with the conclusion that no value leaves 0-1.
The same formula is rerun on India's real numbers, row by row, so the abstract method becomes a worked sheet ending in 0.726.
Two education indicators become one index by an explicit 'we need only one value, so average them' step.

teaching_weak.why: Education results are left as x and y; the learner never sees 11.9/18 = 0.661 or 6.7/15 = 0.447 or their average.
Logs are introduced with 'the formula will not work here' and no reason (diminishing value of extra income); the income index (about 0.63) is never stated.
Made-up indices are attached to a real country (Bulgaria), which can be remembered as fact.
A 30-second run-on sentence for the clamping rule, read fast with no pause.
Ends on a judgement ('how far behind') with no recap of the five-step method.
